harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Restored branch_ledger and configured durable MariaDB replication from node1 to read-only node2. Replication catch-up, write protection, data integrity, and persistence through sequential node restarts were verified.
actions_performed: Installed RHEL 10 AppStream MariaDB 10.11.18 without changing the OS or kernel.
Restored the original ledger rows 1001/12.50 and 1002/-3.25; preserved the staged export unchanged.
Configured node1 as the sole writer with row-based binary logging.
Configured node2 as a read-only replica with relay-log recovery.
Created a node2-restricted replication-only account without exposing its credential.
Verified committed replication using row 1003 and disconnect catch-up using rows 1004–1005.
Restarted node2 and node1 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and complete recovery.
Removed temporary credential/probe files after configuration.

evidence.summary: Both nodes contain five identical unique rows totaling 173.90, including the original IDs and amounts. The export remains at the requested path with SHA-256 fcd54ac91dff5010c8dda0ddfa5cf2586d2d172456c7ca8ca33d0bffabc73700.
ledger_repl is restricted to node2's address and has REPLICATION SLAVE privilege while SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, and DROP privileges are disabled.
Committed row 1003/47.75 arrived on node2, which reached source position 1663 with both threads running and zero lag.

evidence.requirement: Replica disconnect and lossless, duplicate-free catch-up
evidence.summary: Node2 was disconnected at three rows and position 1663. Node1 committed rows 1004–1005, then node2 resumed to five rows, five distinct IDs, total 173.90, and position 1955 without errors.

evidence.requirement: Node2 is a read-only application replica; node1 is sole writer
evidence.summary: Node1 reports read_only=0 and node2 read_only=1. A non-administrative node2 client could read but its insert failed with MariaDB error 1290; read_only remained ON and the row count stayed unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel preserved
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.

Healthy baseline boot ID 7223d5b7-fa56-4ff3-acee-959a5cf5f146, native reboot acknowledgement, connection reset, changed boot ID 9e467172-79fb-4906-b1f6-3d535cf2a9b6, and complete service/data/replication recovery were directly observed.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart persistence and cluster recovery
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 180a78a0-8a84-45ff-82f1-cd734208a369, native reboot acknowledgement, connection reset, changed boot ID fa5666da-a4e2-46e9-9efe-e5b1d6a2aeac, source recovery, and automatic replica reconnection to mariadb-bin.000002 position 344 with zero lag were directly observed.

attempts.summary: Restored branch_ledger and configured durable MariaDB replication from node1 to read-only node2. Replication catch-up, write protection, data integrity, and persistence through sequential node restarts were verified.
